records.title: The Weight Of Words
records.statementTitle: 4th Virginia Tech High School Programming Contest 2017, Problem F — The Weight Of Words
records.identity: Original contest PDF explicitly identifies Problem F as The Weight Of Words; title and Kattis slug match
records.observed: A game asks a player to construct a lowercase word with a specified length and sum of letter weights; the problem asks an AI to find any valid word or report impossible.
records.excerpt: Justin likes to play a game called “Weight of Words.” In this game, a player must find words of a given length and a given weight.
records.inputOutput: Input: target length and total letter weight. Output: any lowercase word satisfying both, or impossible.
records.constraints: 0 < l ≤ 40; 0 < w ≤ 1,000; letters a-z have weights 1-26.
records.scenarioNotes: Officially verified, but compact single-constraint word construction. Exclude from long-scenario quota; retain as ordinary practice.

records.title: Counting Subsequences (Hard)
records.identity: Official IPSC archive identifies Problem C; the Kattis candidate slug subseqhard is consistent with the hard data set C2, but live Kattis page remains blocked
records.observed: Given a sequence of integers, count continuous subsequences whose sum is exactly 47, framed as a humorous 47-society claim.
records.excerpt: We will call a continuous subsequence of S interesting if the sum of its terms is equal to 47.
records.inputOutput: Input: multiple test cases with sequence length and integer sequence. Output: count of interesting contiguous subsequences.
records.constraints: The accessible page specifies the general task and data-set links but does not expose full numeric limits in the statement body inspected; hard dataset C2 link is explicitly present.
records.scenarioNotes: The narrative is a short numerical joke and the task is a standard contiguous-subarray count. Exclude from long-scenario quota; ordinary prefix-sum practice.

records.title: Perket
records.identity: Original COCI contest PDF identifies Task PERKET and provides the statement; title and Kattis slug match
records.observed: Cooks choose a nonempty subset of ingredients. Sourness multiplies across selected ingredients while bitterness sums; choose the subset minimizing the absolute difference.
records.excerpt: For perket to be what it is, cooks must carefully choose the ingredients to get the fullest taste possible
records.inputOutput: Input: ingredient count and each ingredient's sourness and bitterness. Output: minimum possible absolute difference.
records.constraints: 1 ≤ N ≤ 10; if all ingredients are used, both aggregate sourness and bitterness are less than 1,000,000,000.
records.scenarioNotes: Official source verified, but the narrative is a short cooking wrapper around a small subset-enumeration task. Exclude from long-scenario quota; ordinary brute-force practice.
